records.text: PETN is the main component in military and commercial blasting caps, each of which contains less than one gram and can cause major damage.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #5 (Ep VMNWMXX1vO8)

appearances.snippet: It's the main component in military and commercial blasting caps. ... Each blasting cap has less than one gram of PETN and deals major damage.

verification.notes: Authoritative sources show standard detonators commonly use PETN as the secondary or output charge and give representative charges of about 0.45 to 0.60 grams, below one gram. But blasting-cap designs vary, including military caps using RDX or PETN, so the universal military-and-commercial wording and generalized damage claim are too broad.

sources.title: United Nations standard detonator specifications
sources.relevance: Specifies a standard detonator secondary PETN charge of 0.60 grams.

sources.title: National Academies report on detonators
sources.relevance: Explains that detonator output charge is typically PETN while the priming charge can use other compounds.

records.text: Shaped charges are common in improvised explosive devices, copper is their most common material, and even a wine bottle can be used to make one.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #5 (Ep VMNWMXX1vO8)

appearances.snippet: As far as the shaped charge, it is very common in IEDs, and copper is the most common. ... But to give you a sense of how easy it is, you can use a wine bottle to make one as well.

verification.notes: Authoritative mine-action references document shaped-charge IEDs made with copper jet-forming liners and an improvised shaped charge made from a wine bottle and plastic explosive. NIST also defines the metal-lined directional effect. The compound technical claim is supported.

sources.title: ICRC Weapon Contamination Manual Book I
sources.relevance: Documents a shaped-charge IED made from a wine bottle and plastic explosive.

sources.title: GICHD IED Clearance Good Practice Guide
sources.relevance: Documents shaped charges using copper jet-forming cone liners, including locally produced IED-clearance charges.

records.text: My technical friends and I believe Charlie Kirk was hit by the microphone rather than a gun, although we could be biased because we work with improvised explosive devices.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #5 (Ep VMNWMXX1vO8)

appearances.snippet: I know this won't help progress your theories, but me, along with my tech friends, all believe it was the mic. ... We could definitely be biased since we deal with IEDs, but I just thought that you should know that a lot of people who deal with rifles and improvised explosives do not believe it was from a gun.

verification.notes: The episode reads an anonymous message asserting this belief, but the sender and claimed technical credentials cannot be authenticated. Current official evidence alleges a firearm shot, and no forensic source supports a microphone device, so the private opinion has no verifiable evidentiary basis.
